entries.title: 'Broadview Six' judge set to hear high-stakes arguments over feds' apparent misconduct
entries.summary: <p>A highly anticipated hearing with little precedent at the Dirksen Federal Courthouse is set to play out Thursday, when a judge is expected to hear arguments over the potential consequences of alleged prosecutorial misconduct in the politically charged case of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/27/broadview-six-boutros-chicago" target="_blank" >“Broadview Six.”</a></p><p>U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros’ office has been in crisis ever since U.S. District Judge April Perry in May <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/05/21/broadview-ice-protest-grand-jury-transcript-kat-abughazaleh-trump" target="_blank" >revealed apparent wrongdoing</a> by Boutros’ staff in its felony prosecution<b> </b>of six Operation Midway Blitz protesters, most of whom had ties to Democratic politics in the Chicago area.</p><p>The prosecutor who took the brunt of the criticism, Sheri<b> </b>Mecklenburg, has now retired<b> </b>in order to defend herself. She <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/09/25/broadview-six-boutros-mecklenburg" target="_blank" >blasted Boutros<b> </b>last week</a>, saying she followed his team’s<b> </b>direction<b> </b>“at every turn” in the case — adding that Boutros “personally directed”<b> </b>a felony prosecution over her objection that it “was better suited to misdemeanor charges.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/27/broadview-six-boutros-chicago" >What to know about the ‘Broadview Six’ scandal rocking Chicago’s federal courthouse</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>Mecklenburg is accused of three types of misconduct: speaking with grand jurors outside the grand jury room, putting her own credibility on the line to secure charges<b> </b>and excusing grand jurors who disagreed with the case — a claim she’s denied.</p><p>Meanwhile, Boutros’ office has also been accused of a cover-up. That’s because Mecklenburg’s alleged misconduct was redacted out of transcripts<b> </b>given to Perry<b> </b>earlier this year<b> </b>by the feds. The redactions were made after Mecklenburg left the case.</p><p>Now, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/17/broadview-six-judge-april-perry-trump-vance" target="_blank" >Perry must decide</a> whether to appoint an independent special counsel or hear testimony during a separate hearing to help get to the bottom of the “Broadview Six” scandal. It’s unclear whether she will hand down her ruling Thursday or take more time to think about it.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-dc0000" name="image-dc0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/89f0dd5/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4104x2303+0+213/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F57%2Fe5%2Fdc4d63eae5b743c7b018326d9188%2Fmerlin-76298870.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/95717a0/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4104x2303+0+213/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F57%2Fe5%2Fdc4d63eae5b743c7b018326d9188%2Fmerlin-76298870.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/d7cde1e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4104x2303+0+213/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F57%2Fe5%2Fdc4d63eae5b743c7b018326d9188%2Fmerlin-76298870.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Dirksen Federal Courthouse, 219 S. Dearborn St." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/d7cde1e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4104x2303+0+213/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F57%2Fe5%2Fdc4d63eae5b743c7b018326d9188%2Fmerlin-76298870.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b6441ed/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4104x2303+0+213/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F57%2Fe5%2Fdc4d63eae5b743c7b018326d9188%2Fmerlin-76298870.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/d7cde1e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4104x2303+0+213/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F57%2Fe5%2Fdc4d63eae5b743c7b018326d9188%2Fmerlin-76298870.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>The Dirksen Federal Courthouse at 219 S. Dearborn St.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Sun-Times file</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Either way, the situation is unlike any faced by Boutros’ recent predecessors.</p><p>The hearing is sure to draw a large crowd to Perry’s courtroom on the 17th floor<b> </b>of the Dirksen courthouse. The former defendants in the case will likely be among them. So will members of the legal community who’ve watched the scandal tarnish the reputation of what was once considered a top tier U.S. attorney’s office.</p><p>Boutros has acknowledged that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/05/boutros-broadview-six-perry" target="_blank" >“mistakes were made.”</a><b> </b>But he said he’s implemented reforms to prevent them from happening again. The Justice Department has also denied<b> </b>that Mecklenburg recommended misdemeanor charges, insisting she listed a felony as the “strongest charge.”</p><p>But Boutros also faces questions about when he learned of Mecklenburg’s missteps. Though he said he learned about much of what happened in April, he later acknowledged<b> </b>receiving a transcript last October that documented some of the alleged wrongdoing.</p><p>The saga began with a Sept. 26, 2025, demonstration in Broadview<b> </b>against Midway Blitz, the Trump administration deportation campaign that rocked the Chicago area last fall. Prosecutors alleged that a crowd pushed and damaged a federal agent’s SUV as he drove toward an immigration holding facility in the western suburb.</p><p>From that crowd, only six people were charged. Grand jurors accused them of conspiring<b> </b>to impede<b> </b>the agent,<b> </b>leveling a felony charge that threatened a maximum of six years in prison.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/06/01/broadview-six-midway-blitz-abughazaleh-straw-rabbit-perry-trump-ice-crime" target="_blank" >Accused were</a> then-congressional candidate Boutros’ office last year <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/tracker-federal-prosecutions-chicago-status-trumps-immigration-blitz-ice" target="_blank" >collapsed without a conviction</a>, but not in such spectacular fashion as the “Broadview Six” case.</p><p>Prosecutors first dropped charges against two of the six, Sharp and Walsh, in March. They did so after Sharp <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/01/06/cook-county-board-candidate-suspends-campaign-to-fight-indictment" target="_blank" >dropped her campaign</a> for Cook County Board to focus on her legal defense.</p><p>Then, the case seemed to deteriorate further when prosecutors <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/04/29/broadview-ice-crime-chicago-trump-kat-abughezaleh" target="_blank" >dropped the felony conspiracy indictment</a><b> </b>that still threatened the remaining four. The feds said they’d take the four to trial on misdemeanors instead.</p><p>But Boutros’ office only dropped the felony charge after<b> </b>Perry<b> </b>asked to see unredacted transcripts<b> </b>from the grand jury proceedings. Once the feds dropped the felony — and the grand jury’s indictment — the judge agreed the transcripts were irrelevant.</p><p>That raised the suspicions of defense attorneys, though. They urged Perry to look at the unredacted transcripts, finally convincing her to do so days before the trial. Perry later said she was “incredibly shocked”<b> </b>by what she’d found and flagged Mecklenburg’s alleged misconduct.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/05/21/broadview-ice-protest-grand-jury-transcript-kat-abughazaleh-trump" >‘Broadview Six’ charges dropped as Chicago’s top federal prosecutor admits case was tainted by misconduct</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>Damage quickly spread after Perry revealed those allegations May 21. Attorneys <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/05/22/broadview-six-federal-prosecutors-misconduct-tainted-cases-reviewed" target="_blank" >began reviewing other cases</a> handled by Mecklenburg, most notably a pair of prosecutions tied to Loretto Hospital.</p><p>U.S. District Judge Sharon Johnson Coleman, who presides over one of those cases, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/10/hearing-in-loretto-hospital-case-could-address-claims-of-prosecutors-misconduct-if-feds-dont-drop-it" target="_blank" >threatened to hold her own hearing</a> once similar allegations surfaced there. Rather than go forward with the hearing, Boutros’ office <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/11/broadview-six-grand-jury-misconduct-federal-prosecutors-drop-charges-loretto-hospital-covid-fraud" target="_blank" >permanently dropped<b> </b>criminal charges</a><b> </b>against two defendants.</p><p>In all, at least 10 people have seen criminal charges against them evaporate as a result of the allegations against Mecklenburg. More could follow.</p><p>Meanwhile, credibility issues surfaced even in seemingly unrelated cases. After a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/19/shooting-fbi-atf-hotaling-boutros-country-club-hills" target="_blank" >video surfaced</a><b> </b>in June that appeared to contradict an FBI special agent’s sworn affidavit, U.S. Magistrate Judge<b> </b>Keri<b> </b>Holleb<b> </b>Hotaling<b> </b><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/18/boutros-holleb-hotaling-atf-country-club-hills" target="_blank" >told lawyers during a hearing</a>, “this court is very concerned that I cannot rely on the information that is provided to me either from the U.S. Attorney’s Office or from agents.”</p><p>U.S. Magistrate Judge Laura<b> </b>McNally<b> </b>also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/07/03/judge-orders-u-s-attorney-boutros-into-court-over-potential-violations-of-seal-order" target="_blank" >summoned Boutros into court</a> in July, finding that he’d <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/07/09/judge-finds-chicagos-embattled-u-s-attorney-violated-secrecy-order-in-tren-de-aragua-case" target="_blank" >violated<b> </b>a secrecy order</a> governing a case<b> </b>involving the Tren de Aragua<b> </b>gang<b> </b>when he participated in a press conference with then-Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche<b> </b>and FBI Director Kash Patel.</p><p>But no judge has yet to drill into the details of the “Broadview Six” scandal. Not since May 21, when Perry reminded prosecutors of the trust that had been placed in their hands. She told them, “your sole goal is to do justice. Your client is justice itself.”</p><p>“That trust,” she said, “has been broken.”</p>

entries.title: What to know about the Illinois comptroller race between Bryan Drew and state Rep. Margaret Croke
entries.summary: <p>In the Illinois comptroller’s race, incumbent Susana Mendoza decided to put her efforts solely into the Chicago mayor’s race, leaving uncontested Republican Bryan Drew to face state Rep. Margaret Croke (D-12th) in the race for the state’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/02/06/what-to-know-about-illinois-comptroller-primary" target="_blank" ><u>chief financial office</u></a>.</p><h3>What does the state comptroller do?</h3><p>The Illinois comptroller is the state’s chief financial officer. The office manages the state’s fiscal accounts, records all transactions, pays bills and reviews all expenditures and contracts. The comptroller also chairs the State Employees’ Retirement System Board and sits on the Illinois State Board of Investment, helping manage pensions for state employees. The comptroller also issues financial reports about the state’s fiscal affairs. In addition to managing the state’s finances, the office regulates cemeteries and handles the fiduciary protection of cemetery funds meant for the maintenance of grave sites in Illinois.</p><h3>Who is Margaret Croke, the Democratic candidate?</h3><p>Croke is a Chicago area state representative from Lincoln Park billing herself as a moderate Democrat. She says she wants to help modernize the office by creating a transparency system in which residents can see the path of public dollars from appropriation to payment, as well as moving the regulation of funeral home licensing solely under the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation.</p><p>Croke — who was backed by a contingent of Springfield Democrats, including Gov. JB Pritzker — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/03/17/illinois-comptroller-democratic-primary-results" target="_blank" ><u>landed nearly 35% of the vote</u></a> in a four-way race during the March 17 Democratic primary, beating out more progressive candidates with boosts from <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/03/19/margaret-croke-democratic-primary-victory-illinois-comptroller-karina-villa-stephanie-kifowit-holly-kim" target="_blank" ><u>suburban and downstate counties</u></a>. She <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/03/19/margaret-croke-democratic-primary-victory-illinois-comptroller-karina-villa-stephanie-kifowit-holly-kim" target="_blank" ><u>raised $1.8 million in the primary</u></a>.</p><p>She has pointed to her statehouse ties as a positive, as well as her time on the House Revenue and Finance Committee and as chair of the Financial Institutions Committee.</p><p>“My experience has given me a deep understanding of how the public sector ecosystem works, which will help ensure that the most fiscally sound decisions are being made on behalf of taxpayers and those who are most in need,” Croke said in response to a Sun-Times candidate questionnaire.</p><h3>Who is Bryan Drew, the Republican candidate?</h3><p>Drew is a private attorney and cafe owner from downstate Benton. He ended the first quarter of fundraising with just more than $54,000. He and Mendoza have both criticized Croke for taking money from Pritzker and billionaire business executive Michael Sacks, questioning her independence given the donations. After the March primary, Drew said Croke is Pritzker’s “hand-picked candidate” and called her endorsements from the governor and Emanuel "Chris" Welch, Illinois speaker of the house, a “conflict of interest.”</p><p>“My opponent won’t hold any of these politicians accountable, not when she wants to keep climbing the political ladder. Illinoisans deserve better,” Drew <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/03/19/margaret-croke-democratic-primary-victory-illinois-comptroller-karina-villa-stephanie-kifowit-holly-kim" >said in March</a>.</p><p>"Though limited in his experience in state government and finance," Capitol News Illinois <a class="Link" href="https://capitolnewsillinois.com/news/replacing-mendoza-candidates-vie-to-be-states-first-new-comptroller-in-a-decade/" target="_blank" >wrote this week</a>, "Drew said owning a cafe with his wife has exposed him to the impact of high taxes on small businesses. He said he would use the 'bully pulpit' of the office to act as a watchdog for taxpayers."</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-fe0000" name="module-fe0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>What to Know - Races We’re Watching</h3><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9992ee02-bd07-11f1-93ab-21195d7ab2fe"><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-us-senate-race-juliana-stratton-don-tracy-dick-durbin" ><b>U.S. Senate</b></a>: Juliana Stratton, Don Tracy</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-4th-congressional-district-patty-garcia-chris-getty-lupe-castillo-ed-hershey-us-rep-jesus-chuy-garcia" ><b>U.S. Congress (4th District)</b></a>: Lupe Castillo, Patty García, Chris Getty, Ed Hershey</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-llinois-governor-race-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett" ><b>Governor</b></a>: Darren Bailey, Collin Corbett, JB Pritzker</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-candidates-race-illinois-attorney-general-kwame-raoul-bob-fioretti" ><b>Illinois Attorney General</b></a>: Robert Fioretti, Kwame Raoul</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-comptroller-race-bryan-drew-state-rep-margaret-croke" ><b>Illinois Comptroller</b></a>: Margaret Croke, Bryan Drew </li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-secretary-of-state-race-alexi-giannoulias-diane-harris" ><b>Illinois Secretary of State</b></a>: Alexi Giannoulias, Diane M. entries.title: What to know about the race for Illinois attorney general
entries.summary: <p>Former two-term 2nd Ward Ald. Bob Fioretti has a challenge on his hands in his run against Kwame Raoul, the Democratic incumbent Illinois attorney general since 2019, who won his last two elections by a more than 11-point margin.</p><h3>What does the attorney general do in Illinois?</h3><p>Much like its federal counterpart, the <a class="Link" href="https://illinoisattorneygeneral.gov/about/" target="_blank" >state attorney general’s role</a> involves both advocacy and litigation on behalf of the state and its residents. This includes anything from consumer protection to working with legislators and managing statewide law enforcement. </p><h3>Who is the incumbent, Kwame Raoul?</h3><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2025/05/23/illinois-attorney-general-kwame-raoul-fight-against-donald-trump" >Raoul</a>, the son of Haitian immigrants, started his career as a senior staff attorney for the City Colleges of Chicago, then was a prosecutor with the Cook County state’s attorney’s office. He was a state senator for 14 years, initially appointed to fill the seat left open when Barack Obama was elected to the U.S. Senate. Raoul was first elected attorney general in 2018.</p><p>During his current term, Raoul has joined <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/donald-trump/2026/01/20/trump-one-year-kwame-raoul-illinois-lawsuits-jb-pritzker" >numerous lawsuits</a>, some involving multiple attorneys general office across states, over issues such as the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/money/2026/08/03/illinois-attorney-general-kwame-raoul-lawsuit-trump-tariffs" >Trump administration’s tariffs</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/technology/2026/08/26/meta-illinois-pay-nearly-768-million-multistate-settlement-teen-social-media-addiction" >social media addiction</a> in kids, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/02/11/federal-cuts-hiv-lead-poisoning-prevention-grants-raoul" >cuts to public health grants</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/08/26/illinois-ag-kwame-raoul-lawsuit-postal-service-mail-ballot-rule-midterm-elections" >preserving access to mail-in ballots</a>.</p><h3>Who is challenger Bob Fioretti?</h3><p>Fioretti served as alderman for Chicago's 2nd Ward from 2007 to 2015. He trained as a civil rights attorney and has run for a number of offices since leaving City Council, including unsuccessfully twice for mayor and Cook County state’s attorney, as well as a failed bid at Cook County Board president. </p><p>Fioretti has pointed to unnamed corruption and crime as reason for needing to shake things up in the office, <a class="Link" href="https://www.bobforillinois.com/post/robert-fioretti-a-new-vision-for-illinois-justice" target="_blank" ><u>citing</u></a> his courtroom experience with City Hall's corporation counsel office, plus his time as an assistant Illinois attorney general and alderman, as qualifications for the state’s highest legal officer.</p><h3>What makes the attorney general’s office in Illinois stand out?</h3><p>The Trump administration's moves against Illinois has elevated the attorney general's role to defender of the state’s federal funds. Raoul has filed dozens of lawsuits to protect Illinois from federal funding cutbacks. Raoul, along with other states’ attorneys general, has successfully won the release of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2025/09/24/illinois-wins-suit-on-disaster-relief-funding-held-by-dhs-over-sanctuary-laws" target="_blank" ><u>$2 billion in federal disaster relief funding</u></a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2025/11/04/judge-blocks-trump-administration-transportation-funds" target="_blank" ><u>federal transportation funding</u></a> after the Trump White House held up the money over immigration enforcement.</p><p>Other lawsuits from Raoul's office have restored <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/01/06/appeals-court-kwame-raoul-trump-administration-medical-research" target="_blank" ><u>medical research funding</u></a> cut by the Trump administration and r<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/09/04/illinois-joins-lawsuit-against-second-trump-admin-push-to-cut-federal-funding-for-youth-gender-affirming-care" target="_blank" ><u>eversed a Trump administration attempt</u></a> to cut federal funding from medical institutions providing gender-affirming care to patients under 19.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-c20000" name="module-c20000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>What to Know - entries.title: New Latino anthology of horror stories draws its fright from folklore
entries.summary: <p>What keeps you up at night?</p><p>Is it politics? Money? Climate change? Maybe it’s something more obviously sinister, like murderers and ghosts?</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/entertainment-and-culture/2024/03/15/cynthia-pelayo-forgotten-sisters-book-ghost-stories-chicago" target="_blank" ><u>Cynthia Pelayo</u></a>, a Bram Stoker Award-winning horror novelist from Chicago, asked herself and 16 fellow Latin American authors — living both outside and within the borders of the U.S. — to reflect on that question for a new anthology released this week titled “Something Followed Us Home: Tales of Latiné Horror.”</p><p>In “Something Followed Us Home,” 17 short stories and an introductory foreword begin deep into dark timelines, such as in “Her First Cruise Ship” by Ann Dávila Cardinal, where undead and rotting American tourists stumble through the capital city of Puerto Rico. The book’s foreword is written by Mexican author Brenda Lozano, and editions are available in English and Spanish through a bilingual publisher.</p><p>A man is possessed by a demon in “My Boyfriend” by Gerardo Sámano Córdova. A dog walker meets a famous writer under chilling circumstances in “The Rooftop Revolution of Selly Avilés” by Daniel José Older.</p><p>Pelayo said she has been interested in exploring fear through the literary lenses of Latino authors for years. She said that the collection has been three to four years in the making.</p><p>“There is this consistent thread that I've seen so much … our stories being told and carried generationally, and I really wanted to understand what haunts [these authors],” said <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/books/2025/10/01/marvel-latino-character-white-tiger-revival-chicago-cynthia-pelayo" target="_blank" ><u>Pelayo</u></a>, who was born in Arecibo, Puerto Rico. “Is there a story? Is there a piece of folklore, a family secret?”</p><p>Featuring an array of acclaimed contemporary authors, including Agustina Bazterrica, Isabel Cañas, Leopoldo Goût and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/books/2025/09/03/chicago-public-library-2025-one-book-olga-dies-dreaming-xochitl-gonzalez" target="_blank" ><u>Xochitl Gonzalez,</u></a> whose book “Olga Dies Dreaming" was Chicago’s 2025 citywide read, the horrifying (and sometimes stomach-turning) stories weave together worlds in which human-made horrors and otherworldly ones converge.</p><div Goût.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Beowulf Sheehan; Provided; Barry Brecheisen/For the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Pelayo’s story, “El Jíbaro de Puerto Rico,” is inspired by a real-life massacre that happened in 1937 in Ponce, Puerto Rico. A peaceful march <a class="Link" href="https://www.zinnedproject.org/news/tdih/ponce-massacre/" target="_blank" ><u>turned deadly</u></a> after police opened fire and killed 19 islanders and wounded hundreds more.</p><p>Pelayo did not take submissions for the book, preferring to approach authors herself. “The range of storytelling that came to me was very fascinating,” she said. “There's a very haunting ghost story with Agustina Bazterrica's ‘Blue Flowers,’ which left me stunned after I read that story.” The Argentine author wrote “Tender Is the Flesh,” a 2017 dystopian novel that illustrates a world where animals, especially bovines and avians used for human consumption, have gone extinct.</p><p>Some of Ananda Lima’s fears involve AI and how it has quickly changed the world. She wrote “Specter,” which draws on Brazilian folklore.</p><p>In Lima’s story, the boogeywoman known as Cuca torments a young woman as she tries to navigate college life.</p><p>“Cuca is very much a part of so many people's childhood,” she said. “It's basically a witch creature who has a crocodile head.”</p><p>As she researched Cuca, Lima found links to similar stories from Spain and Portugal and learned about other creatures that helped evolve the tale. “It turned into a story about something that [is] creating a lot of fear and anxiety, which is AI,” Lima said.</p><p>Many aspects of modern technological advancements make Lima nervous or scared, but “letting it simmer through fiction” is always a liberating outlet, she said. Lima divides her time between Chicago and New York City.</p><p>Goût, a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/art/2024/11/08/leopoldo-gout-povos-gallery-west-town-elefante-chicago" target="_blank" ><u>multidisciplinary artist</u></a> from Mexico, wrote the ninth story in the book, “Luz Y Fer.” He was completing his recent novel “Rooted” when Pelayo reached out to him about writing something for the anthology.</p><p>“My work usually starts with details of the character,” Goût said. “Sometimes I make a painting, and then those paintings become a different story. Some of them end up in an art piece, and some of them end up in a book.”</p><p>But the vision for “Luz Y Fer,” a story about twins separated at birth, came to the artist in a “very vivid dream.” Goût thinks it was because he was recently researching Lucifer, a religious figure in Christianity who represents Satan or the Devil after his fall from heaven.</p><p>“Lucifer is a great humanist in some pre-Catholic religions,” Goût said of his findings. The story is meant to flip religious and traditional views on morality on their head, and think of life and situations beyond the frameworks of good and evil.</p><p>“We are products of extraordinary layers of and collisions of culture, and that's what I wanted to do with ‘Luz Y Fer,’” Goût said.</p><p>Pelayo and a handful of authors will appear at a <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/p/Dd1juDNx0Ua/?hl=en" target="_blank" ><u>book launch event Thursday</u></a>, held at Downtown bookshop <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/exileinbookville/?hl=en" target="_blank" ><u>Exile in Bookville</u></a>. That talk will include Lima and Northwestern University English professor Juan Martínez.</p><p>The book was published through Primero Sueño Press, a bilingual <a class="Link" href="https://www.simonandschuster.biz/p/announcing-primero-sueno-press" target="_blank" ><u>publishing house</u></a> from Atria Books and Simon & Schuster that translates to “first dream” press.</p><p>When Pelayo called Goût, she’d barely gotten the publisher's name out before the artist immediately agreed. “‘Yeah, I'm in,’” he said.</p>

entries.title: What to know about Illinois legislative races ahead of the Nov. 3 election
entries.summary: <p>The primary elections in March featured several challenges to Democratic incumbents in the General Assembly, but now that the general election Nov. 3 is almost here many politicians are running unopposed.</p><p>There are still some hotly contested races in the suburbs. However, Democrats appear unlikely to be unseated from their big majorities in the Illinois Senate and Illinois House.</p><p>After the election, lawmakers are expected to meet Nov. 17-19 and Dec. 1-3 for the fall veto session and then the new senators and representatives will head to Springfield for their regular spring session in January.</p><p>Here's what to know.</p><h3>What is the General Assembly?</h3><p>The Illinois General Assembly meets at the state Capitol in Springfield every January to debate and vote on proposed laws, adjourning in May or June. There are 118 members of the Illinois House of Representatives and 59 members of the Illinois Senate.</p><p>Democrats make up 78 of the seats in the Illinois House, giving them a strong majority. All state representatives serve two-year terms with elections on even-numbered years, meaning all the seats are up for a vote in November.</p><p>Illinois Senate races, on the other hand, are staggered. There are 39 seats up for election this year. Similar to the House, Democrats have a super-majority in the Senate, controlling 40 seats to Republicans' 19.</p><p>To locate your state Senate and House districts and learn who is representing you in Springfield, go <a class="Link" href="https://www.elections.il.gov/electionoperations/districtlocator/districtofficialsearchbyaddress.aspx" target="_blank" >here on the Illinois State Board of Elections website</a>. It will also provide information about other political office holders.</p><p>Democrats see opportunities to pick up additional seats, though it likely will only pad their overwhelming dominance in the legislature, something they’ve enjoyed since 2019.</p><p>More than a quarter of the members of the Illinois General Assembly represent Chicago or portions of the city, and the vast majority are Democrats.</p><p>Democratic committees are spending to turn more seats.</p><h3>What are some key races Nov. 3?</h3><p>Several suburban races for Springfield lawmakers are shaping up to be highly competitive fights heading into the Nov. 3 election.</p><p>Among the most interesting races, Rep. Nabeela Syed, a Democrat, is challenging incumbent state Sen. Darby Hills, a Republican appointed to the seat, for the 26th District senate seat. The northwest suburban district includes parts of Cook, Lake, McHenry and Kane counties.</p><p>Syed is completing her second term in the Illinois House after graduating from the University of California Berkeley, while Hills is completing the term of Dan McConchie, who resigned to take a job with a nonprofit organization.</p><p>In September alone, the state Democratic Party and a committee led by Illinois Senate President Don Harmon — with the aim of bolstering Democrats' majority — contributed almost $1 million to Syed. Republican political committees contributed almost $80,000 to Hills in September after giving her more than $300,000 in August.</p><p>In the north suburban Illinois House 52nd District, Democrats see a chance to unseat Republican Martin McLaughlin, who faces Maria Peterson in a rematch. In 2024, McLaughlin eked out a victory against Peterson, beating her by fewer than 50 votes.</p><p>In another rematch a little further from Chicago in north central Illinois, Republican Liz Bishop is challenging incumbent Democrat Amy “Murri” Briel for the 76th House District seat in a race that includes salacious allegations against Briel.</p><p>Bishop, who lost to Briel in 2024 by less than 600 votes, has called out Briel’s character and released a video interview with a former staffer alleging that Briel sexually harassed the woman, fed her a prescription stimulant drug and smoked pot while performing legislative duties.</p><p>Briel denies the allegations and points to a statehouse watchdog investigation that concluded the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/springfield/2026/08/20/amy-briel-laura-jackson-chris-welch-lig-investigation-harassment" >allegations were unfounded.</a></p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-830000" name="module-830000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>What to Know - Races We’re Watching</h3><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9992ee02-bd07-11f1-93ab-21195d7ab2fe"><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-us-senate-race-juliana-stratton-don-tracy-dick-durbin" ><b>U.S. Senate</b></a>: Juliana Stratton, Don Tracy</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-4th-congressional-district-patty-garcia-chris-getty-lupe-castillo-ed-hershey-us-rep-jesus-chuy-garcia" ><b>U.S. Congress (4th District)</b></a>: Lupe Castillo, Patty García, Chris Getty, Ed Hershey</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-llinois-governor-race-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett" ><b>Governor</b></a>: Darren Bailey, Collin Corbett, JB Pritzker</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-candidates-race-illinois-attorney-general-kwame-raoul-bob-fioretti" ><b>Illinois Attorney General</b></a>: Robert Fioretti, Kwame Raoul</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-comptroller-race-bryan-drew-state-rep-margaret-croke" ><b>Illinois Comptroller</b></a>: Margaret Croke, Bryan Drew </li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-secretary-of-state-race-alexi-giannoulias-diane-harris" ><b>Illinois Secretary of State</b></a>: Alexi Giannoulias, Diane M. Harris</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-97th-house-district-race-jessica-dixon-heitman-gabby-shanahan" ><b>Illinois House (District 97)</b></a>: Jessica Dixon Heitman, Gabby Shanahan</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/illinois-statehouse-elections-november-3-senate-house-general-assembly-what-to-know" ><b>More Illinois House Races</b></a></li></ul></div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: How to vote in the November 2026 Illinois general election
entries.summary: <p>Voting is underway in Illinois for the 2026 general election.</p><p>For Chicagoans, at stake will be the election of a Chicago Public Schools board president — a race that features attorney Victor Henderson, Jessica Biggs, a former CPS principal, and Hilario Dominguez, a former CTU deputy political director. Also on the ballot are all 20 seats for the city’s Board of Education. It marks the first time the entire CPS board will be elected by the city’s voters.</p><p>As for non-CPS races, on the ballot will be: candidates for U.S. Senate; Congress, Illinois governor, attorney general, comptroller, treasurer and secretary of state, and the Illinois General Assembly, along with Cook County races, including board president and county commissioners. Outside of Cook, a vast array of races will appear on ballots in the collar counties.</p><p></p><p>Election Day is on Nov. 3, 2026. Here's everything you need to know to cast your vote.</p><h3>Important dates </h3><p></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-70820792-014f-11f1-af2b-6575502a2886"><li><b>Oct. 1:</b> Early voting starts at the downtown Chicago supersite (137 S. State St.) and at the Chicago Board of Elections office (69 W. Washington St., 6th floor).</li><li><b>Oct. 7:</b> First day of grace period for in-person voter registration and voting at election authority and early voting sites. This continues through Election Day.</li><li><b>Oct. 18:</b> Last day for online voter registration.</li><li><b>Oct. 19:</b> 50 ward early voting sites open in Chicago.</li><li><b>Oct. 29:</b> Last day to apply to vote by mail.</li><li><b>Nov. 3:</b> Primary Election Day. Polls are open from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.</li></ul><h3>Are you eligible to vote in Illinois?</h3><p>To vote in the Illinois, you must be the following:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-eb0975b0-b91a-11f1-9f2c-8d8113f0ee8e"><li>U.S. citizen</li><li>18 years or older by the date of the general election</li><li>Resident of the Illinois precinct for at least 30 days</li></ul><h3>Are you registered to vote?</h3><p>To check your voter registration, go to the <a class="Link" href="https://ova.elections.il.gov/RegistrationLookup.aspx" target="_blank" >Illinois State Board of Elections website</a> or the <a class="Link" href="https://chicagoelections.gov/" target="_blank" >Chicago Board of Elections website</a>.</p><p>There are multiple ways to register: <br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-eb0975b1-b91a-11f1-9f2c-8d8113f0ee8e"><li><b>Online:</b> Go to the <a class="Link" href="https://ova.elections.il.gov/" target="_blank" >Illinois State Board of Elections’</a> website. Registration closes 16 days before Election Day.</li><li><b>Municipal offices:</b> Multiple local government offices register voters in-person including the County Clerk's Office, Board of Election Commissions Office, City and Village Offices, Township Offices, Military Recruitment Offices.</li><li><b>Driver's license renewal:</b> When applying for or renewing your driver's license or state ID card at a DMV, you will be asked if you want to register to vote. If you answer yes, you will be required to attest, under penalty of perjury, that you meet the qualifications to register to vote and provide your electronic signature. </li><li><b>Same day in-person:</b> Illinois allows same day registration at early voting sites and on Election Day. Bring at least two forms of ID or proof of residency — such as a passport, driver’s license, lease or mortgage. At least one document must list your current address.</li></ul><h3>What if I recently moved?</h3><p>It is important to register to vote at your current address for a ballot that accurately reflects hyperlocal races like the Chicago School Board. (is there more to add to this?)</p><p></p><h3>Where to vote early in person </h3><p>Early voting sites in the Chicago area open on different dates:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-609d7460-0210-11f1-a803-ebb59b1ce06e"><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicagoelections.gov/voting/early-voting" target="_blank" >City of Chicago</a>: Early voting opens on Oct. 1 at the downtown Chicago supersite (137 S. State St.) and the Chicago Board of Elections office (69 W. Washington St., 6th floor). The 50 ward early voting sites will open in Chicago on Oct. 19.</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.cookcountyclerkil.gov/elections/ways-to-vote/early-voting/early-voting-locations" target="_blank" >Suburban Cook County</a>: Early voting starts Oct. 7 in suburban Cook County, with more locations opening Oct. 19.</li></ul><p>For the collar counties:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-609d9b70-0210-11f1-a803-ebb59b1ce06e"><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.dupagecounty.gov/elected_officials/election_and_voter_information/voting_information/early_voting_locations.php" target="_blank" >DuPage County</a> started early voting Sept. 24 at five locations, according to the DuPage County Clerk's office. Two dozen more early voting sites open in the county starting Oct. 19.</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://clerk.kanecountyil.gov/Elections/Pages/Early-Voting.aspx" target="_blank" >Kane County</a> early voting started on Sept. 24 at the Kane County Clerk's Office in Geneva and at the clerk's Aurora satellite office.</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.kendallcountyil.gov/offices/county-clerk-recorder/election-voter-information" target="_blank" >Kendall County</a> early voting started on Sept. 24 at Kendall County Clerk's Office.</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.lakecountyil.gov/DocumentCenter/View/13400/Early-Voting-Locations-Dates-and-Times" target="_blank" >Lake County</a> started early voting on Sept. 24 at the Lake County Courthouse. More locations will be open Oct. 19, with some shutting down by Oct. 31 while others will carry on through the election. Hours vary location to location.</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.mchenrycountyil.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/123070/639249772220270000" target="_blank" >McHenry County</a> early voting began Sept. 24 at the McHenry County Election Center and more sites open starting Oct. 19.</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.willcountyclerk.gov/elections/early-voting/" target="_blank" >Will County</a> early voting began Sept. 24 at the Will County Clerk’s Office with more sites opening starting Oct. 19.</li></ul><h3>How to vote by mail </h3><p><b>Illinois residents:</b> To receive a mail-in ballot, through the mail via your local election authority. You must apply to <b>vote by mail by 5 p.m. on Oct. 29</b> and your ballot must be postmarked or placed in a dropbox by Election Day — Nov. 3 — in order for it to be counted.</p><p>You also have the option to join the vote-by-mail permanent roster to automatically receive mail-in ballots going forward. If you have voted by mail before, but aren't on the permanent list, you must apply again to vote by mail during the upcoming election.</p><p>If you receive a mail-in ballot but decide you want to vote in person instead, you must bring the mail ballot you received with you to your polling place and turn it over to cast an in-person ballot instead.</p><p>Apply online to vote by mail below:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-efac3d52-0150-11f1-bd7b-9d85d5e88d4c"><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicagoelections.gov/voting/vote-mail" target="_blank" >City of Chicago</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.cookcountyclerkil.gov/elections/ways-to-vote/vote-by-mail" target="_blank" >Suburban Cook County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.dupagecounty.gov/elected_officials/election_and_voter_information/voting_information/vote_by_mail.php" target="_blank" >DuPage County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://clerk.kanecountyil.gov/Elections/Pages/Vote-by-Mail.aspx" target="_blank" >Kane County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.kendallcountyil.gov/offices/county-clerk-recorder/election-voter-information/ballot-by-mail-request" target="_blank" >Kendall County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.lakecountyil.gov/4321/Voting-by-Mail" target="_blank" >Lake County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.mchenrycountyil.gov/departments/county-clerk/elections/vote-by-mail" target="_blank" >McHenry County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.willcountyclerk.gov/elections/vote-by-mail/" target="_blank" >Will County</a></li></ul><h3>Where to vote on Election Day </h3><p>Look up your local voting place <a class="Link" href="https://ova.elections.il.gov/pollingplacelookup.aspx" target="_blank" >here</a>.</p><p>Chicago voters can cast their ballot at the voting supersite at 191 N. Clark St., at their early voting location or their local polling place, which can be found below:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-dae30ac1-0150-11f1-bd7c-c93aa3e988aa"><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicagoelections.gov/voting/your-voter-information" target="_blank" >City of Chicago</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.cookcountyclerkil.gov/elections/your-voter-information" target="_blank" >Suburban Cook County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.dupagecounty.gov/elected_officials/election_and_voter_information/voting_information/voter_lookup_tool.php" target="_blank" >DuPage County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://clerk.kanecountyil.gov/Elections/Pages/Election-Day-Voting.aspx" target="_blank" >Kane County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="http://kendall.il.electionconsole.com/voter-lookup.php" target="_blank" >Kendall County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.lakecountyil.gov/351/Voter-Power-for-Registered-Voters" target="_blank" >Lake County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://mchenry-il.connect4.clarityelections.com/sample-ballot-locator/#Search" target="_blank" >McHenry County</a></li><li><a class="Link" href="https://www.willcountyclerk.gov/elections/voter-services/precinct-lookup/" target="_blank" >Will County</a></li></ul><h3>What to remember while voting </h3><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-390400bb-f7aa-11f0-a45d-2df28ea0263e"><li>Ballots in other languages are available. Chicago and Cook County polling locations have voting machines that offer audio ballots in Arabic, Chinese (audio in Mandarin dialect), Gujarati, Hindi, Korean, Polish, Russian, Spanish, Tagalog, Ukrainian and Urdu.</li></ul><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-390400bc-f7aa-11f0-a45d-2df28ea0263e"><li>You can bring notes, <a class="Link" href="https://www.elections.il.gov/Main/FAQ.aspx#Election-q01" target="_blank" >sample ballots</a> and endorsements with you into a polling booth.</li></ul><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-390400bd-f7aa-11f0-a45d-2df28ea0263e"><li>You can bring children with you to vote.</li></ul><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-390400be-f7aa-11f0-a45d-2df28ea0263e"><li>If you're blind, physically disabled or unable to read or write, you can ask an election judge, friend, family member or another voter to help you complete your ballot. But that helper can't be from your employer or union, and that person also cannot influence your vote and cannot fill out your ballot without your expressed consent.</li></ul><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-390400bf-f7aa-11f0-a45d-2df28ea0263e"><li>Illinois prohibits "<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/letters-to-the-editor/2025/04/19/ballot-selfie-illinois-filmmakers-chicago-emmanuel-camarillo-teachers-real-id-easter-donald-trump" >ballot selfies</a>" — a Class 4 felony punishable by up to three years in prison and a $25,000 fine in Illinois — so you can’t post a photo of a completed ballot on social media. However, there are no laws against taking and posting a selfie with your "I Voted" sticker.</li></ul>

entries.title: What to know about the 4th Congressional District race to replace U.S. Rep. Jesus 'Chuy' Garcia
entries.summary: <p>A former congressional chief of staff, a suburban mayor, a teacher and a 43-year resident of the 4th Congressional District are all vying for the seat left vacant by U.S. Rep. Jesus "Chuy" Garcia's retirement.</p><h3>So what?</h3><p>García’s last-minute ballot switch — helping his then-chief of staff Patty García get enough petitions to take his spot on the Democratic ballot — has nabbed a lot of attention about the race. Chuy García's move was widely panned as a maneuver that critics called a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2025/11/03/jesus-chuy-garcia-reelection-dropping-out-chief-of-staff-running" target="_blank" >coronation and a Chicago machine play</a>. The congressman filed petitions with the Illinois State Board of Elections to run for his 4th Congressional District seat on Oct. 27, but his chief of staff filed petitions just ahead of 5 p.m. Nov. 3, the deadline for filing. Chuy García later pulled his petitions. He was also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2025/11/13/chuy-garcia-stepping-down-patty-garcia-successor-march-primary-marie-gluesenkamp-perez" target="_blank" >reprimanded on the House floor.</a></p><p> Patty García, no relation to the congressman, is trying to move forward into the general election and is building major Democratic support, both in Illinois and in Washington. Lyons Mayor Christopher Getty is running as the lone independent candidate, after two candidates — Ald. Byron Sigcho-Lopez (25th) and Mayra Macias failed to submit the required number of signatures. Lupe Castillo is the Republican candidate. Ed Hershey, a teacher, is the Working Class Party candidate. </p><h3>What does a U.S. representative do?</h3><p>Representatives vote on federal laws, advocate for their districts and work to secure federal funding and other resources for constituents. They serve two-year terms. </p><h3>Who are the candidates?</h3><p><b>Patty Garcia, </b>who has a Ph.D. in education policy,<b> </b>worked in Chuy Garcia’s office since 2019. She resigned as his chief of staff in November 2025. She has vowed to continue his work fighting for immigrant and working-class families in the Southwest Side district that stretches to the western suburbs.</p><p><b>Chris Getty</b> has served as mayor of Lyons since 2009 and is the town supervisor Lyons Township. He's also a licensed insurance producer. Getty says his priorities include improving the cost of living, immigration and public safety and government accountability. </p><p><b>Lupe Castillo</b> says she’s running on a platform of “pro-family values and policies." She says she’s the only candidate that “will protect women’s sports and girl’s bathrooms,” and who would support law enforcement over criminals. She’s also supportive of voter ID and school choice. She has lived in the district for 43 years. </p><p><b>Ed Hershey</b> has been teaching at Lindblom Math and Science Academy in West Englewood for 16 years and says his work in schools has shown him how a lack of resources can affect students. He’s also served as a union representative and ran for alderman of the 25th Ward in 2015.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-ea0000" name="module-ea0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>What to Know - Races We’re Watching</h3><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9992ee02-bd07-11f1-93ab-21195d7ab2fe"><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-us-senate-race-juliana-stratton-don-tracy-dick-durbin" ><b>U.S. Senate</b></a>: Juliana Stratton, Don Tracy</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-4th-congressional-district-patty-garcia-chris-getty-lupe-castillo-ed-hershey-us-rep-jesus-chuy-garcia" ><b>U.S. Congress (4th District)</b></a>: Lupe Castillo, Patty García, Chris Getty, Ed Hershey</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-llinois-governor-race-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett" ><b>Governor</b></a>: Darren Bailey, Collin Corbett, JB Pritzker</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-candidates-race-illinois-attorney-general-kwame-raoul-bob-fioretti" ><b>Illinois Attorney General</b></a>: Robert Fioretti, Kwame Raoul</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-comptroller-race-bryan-drew-state-rep-margaret-croke" ><b>Illinois Comptroller</b></a>: Margaret Croke, Bryan Drew </li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-secretary-of-state-race-alexi-giannoulias-diane-harris" ><b>Illinois Secretary of State</b></a>: Alexi Giannoulias, Diane M. entries.title: What to know about the race for Illinois governor
entries.summary: <p>Incumbent Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker, seeking a rare third term as Illinois governor, squares off with Republican nominee Darren Bailey and independent candidate Collin Corbett.</p><h3><b>Why does this sound familiar?</b></h3><p>Pritzker was first elected in 2018, and this year’s contest presents a rematch of his 2022 reelection victory when he <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2022/11/8/23448412/j-b-pritzker-declares-victory-over-gop-challenger-darren-bailey" target="_blank" ><u>beat Bailey</u></a> by nearly 13 percentage points.</p><h3><b>Why does this race matter?</b></h3><p>The governor serves as the state’s chief executive officer, helping set the legislative agenda for the Illinois General Assembly, proposing state budgets, appointing leaders of state agencies and advocating for federal resources, among other sweeping responsibilities.</p><h3><b>Who is JB Pritzker?</b></h3><p>Pritzker, a billionaire heir to the Hyatt hotel fortune, is a former entrepreneur and philanthropist who has championed a series of progressive causes during two terms at a tumultuous point in the state’s history, navigating the COVID-19 pandemic and regularly butting heads with President Donald Trump’s administration.</p><p>Widely considered a potential 2028 <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/07/09/pritzker-for-president-handicapping-the-illinois-governors-political-future" target="_blank" ><u>presidential contender</u></a>, Pritzker would be the first Illinois governor elected to a third term since former Republican Gov. Jim Thompson won the third of his four terms in 1982.</p><h3><b>Who is Darren Bailey?</b></h3><p>Bailey is a farmer and former state senator from southern Illinois who elevated his profile as a vociferous critic of COVID-19 restrictions implemented by Pritzker early in the pandemic, maintaining his hardline conservative base in downstate regions en route to a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2022/6/28/23187510/darren-bailey-richard-irvin-pritzker-republican-governors-race-jesse-sullivan" target="_blank" ><u>second straight</u></a> gubernatorial nomination.</p><p>Trump endorsed Bailey’s 2022 campaign and encouraged him to stay in the 2026 race in the face of immense personal tragedy <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2025/11/11/darren-bailey-gop-primary-governor-race-illinois-helicopter-tragedy" target="_blank" ><u>last year</u></a> when a helicopter crash claimed the lives of Bailey’s son, daughter-in-law and two grandchildren.</p><h3><b>Who is Collin Corbett?</b></h3><p>Corbett is a moderate Republican political consultant running as an <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/09/09/collin-corbett-illinois-governor-independent-candidate-november-midterm-election" target="_blank" ><u>independent</u></a>. He collected 37,000 signatures to get on the ballot. </p><p>A fiscal conservative who supports abortion rights and opposes much of the Trump agenda, the millennial candidate says he offers middle ground in a polarized political climate.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-a00000" name="module-a00000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>What to Know - Races We’re Watching</h3><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9992ee02-bd07-11f1-93ab-21195d7ab2fe"><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-us-senate-race-juliana-stratton-don-tracy-dick-durbin" ><b>U.S. Senate</b></a>: Juliana Stratton, Don Tracy</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-4th-congressional-district-patty-garcia-chris-getty-lupe-castillo-ed-hershey-us-rep-jesus-chuy-garcia" ><b>U.S. Congress (4th District)</b></a>: Lupe Castillo, Patty García, Chris Getty, Ed Hershey</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-llinois-governor-race-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett" ><b>Governor</b></a>: Darren Bailey, Collin Corbett, JB Pritzker</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-candidates-race-illinois-attorney-general-kwame-raoul-bob-fioretti" ><b>Illinois Attorney General</b></a>: Robert Fioretti, Kwame Raoul</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-comptroller-race-bryan-drew-state-rep-margaret-croke" ><b>Illinois Comptroller</b></a>: Margaret Croke, Bryan Drew </li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-secretary-of-state-race-alexi-giannoulias-diane-harris" ><b>Illinois Secretary of State</b></a>: Alexi Giannoulias, Diane M. Harris</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-97th-house-district-race-jessica-dixon-heitman-gabby-shanahan" ><b>Illinois House (District 97)</b></a>: Jessica Dixon Heitman, Gabby Shanahan</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/illinois-statehouse-elections-november-3-senate-house-general-assembly-what-to-know" ><b>More Illinois House Races</b></a></li></ul></div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: What to know about Illinois' 97th House District race between Jessica Dixon Heitman and Gabby Shanahan
entries.summary: <p>Appointed state Rep. Jessica Dixon Heitman, D-Plainfield, seeks election to a full term against Republican nominee Gabby Shanahan, who narrowly lost in 2024 to ex-state Rep. Harry Benton before his resignation amid sexual harassment allegations.</p><h3><b>What’s important about this race?</b></h3><p>This far southwest suburban district provides one of the few competitive races on Illinois’ heavily gerrymandered political map, and it’s at the center of the latest sexual harassment scandal to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/springfield/2026/08/05/welch-benton-harassment-working-group-cassidy" target="_blank" ><u>rattle Springfield</u></a>.</p><p>Illinois House Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch knew of a complaint against Benton shortly after the ex-lawmaker took office in 2023, but the speaker still directed $1.4 million to Benton’s reelection campaign.</p><p>Facing complaints from two more women, Benton resigned this summer, admitting no wrongdoing. Will and Kendall county party leaders appointed Dixon Heitman to fill his seat.</p><h3><b>What do state representatives do?</b></h3><p>Members of the Illinois House propose and vote on bills to become state law, advocating for resources for their districts.</p><h3><b>Who is Jessica Dixon Heitman?</b></h3><p>Dixon Heitman is a Democratic former statehouse media relations staffer and a public relations consultant who briefly worked as a contract employee in Benton’s office, but left after noticing “red flags” in his behavior, she <a class="Link" href="https://fwrnews.com/2026/07/21/38732/" target="_blank" ><u>has said</u></a>.</p><p>She’s also a granddaughter of the late former U.S. Sen. Alan Dixon.</p><h3><b>Who is Gabby Shanahan?</b></h3><p>Shanahan is a Republican court-appointed special advocate for children in the Kendall County court system, and a former member of the Kendall County Board of Health.</p><p>In 2024, she lost to Benton by about four percentage points in a district that supported Kamala Harris by roughly the same margin over President Donald Trump in that year's election.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-9d0000" name="module-9d0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>What to Know - entries.title: What to know about the U.S. Senate race to replace Sen. Dick Durbin
entries.summary: <p>After defeating two Democratic members of Congress and eight other candidates in a heated March primary, Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton faces former Illinois Republican Party Chair Don Tracy in the Nov. 3 election for the U.S. Senate seat left vacant by Sen. Dick Durbin's retirement.</p><p>Stratton won the primary on the heels of a late campaign surge and millions in support from longtime running mate Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker. Her momentum was enough to overcome an astounding $29 million Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi spent on campaign ads. </p><p>It began with a commanding debate performance in January and was amplified by strong ads in the final weeks of the campaign. Stratton outperformed Krishnamoorthi in the Metro East region, Sangamon County, Chicago and some suburbs of Cook County — which took away any lead the congressman had in some collar counties. </p><p>Republicans haven't won a statewide seat in Illinois in 12 years, when Pritzker unseated GOP former Gov. Bruce Rauner, a close ally of Tracy. But Tracy says he's running to give a voice to the millions of Republicans in the state. </p><h3>So what?</h3><p>Durbin's retirement announcement in April 2025 caused a seismic shift in Illinois politics, opening up the U.S. Senate seat he has held since 1996. That announcement also opened up the 2nd Congressional seat, with Rep. Robin Kelly opting to run for the primary, and the 8th Congressional District, where Krishnamoorthi also opted to run. Stratton's March victory also served as a test of Pritzker’s political might as he explores his own future, with the Democratic governor endorsing her just a day after she announced her run in April.</p><h3>How long is the term?</h3><p>The seat’s six-year term will begin January 2027.</p><h3>What does a U.S. senator do?</h3><p>Senators take action on bills, resolutions, amendments, motions, nominations and treaties by voting. Most importantly, they can confirm U.S. presidential appointments, approve or reject treaties and can convict or exonerate impeachment cases — which could be a factor during President Donald Trump’s second term.</p><h3>Who are the candidates?</h3><h4></h4><p> Stratton served in the Illinois General Assembly before Pritzker tapped her to serve as his running mate in 2018. As lieutenant governor, Stratton helped oversee the Illinois Birth Equity Initiative, which requires insurers that provide state health care plans to cover pregnancy and postpartum services for up to 12 months after the end of pregnancy. Stratton helped spearhead maternal health discussions with doulas and midwives with the aim of improving birth equity and maternal health outcomes for Black women. She also led the Justice, Equity and Opportunity Initiative, which aimed to centralize and coordinate criminal justice reforms across state agencies. Illinois will see its fourth Black senator in the Senate if Stratton wins the reliably blue seat in November. She would also become the sixth Black woman to serve in the current Senate.</p><p>Among her campaign platforms, Stratton said she supports a $25 minimum wage, abolishing ICE, Medicare for All and a federal tax increase on individuals earning $1 million or more annually.</p><p> Tracy is a Springfield attorney and businessman. He served as the chair of the Illinois Republican Party from 2021 until his resignation in July 2024. He is also the former chairman of the Illinois Gaming Board, appointed in 2015. Tracy pointed to Republican infighting for his exit from his chairmanship of the state GOP party in 2024 after three and a half years, a tenure that saw the party’s influence wane further in the state as its base moves further right. Tracy ran unsuccessfully for lieutenant governor in 2010 — and won a Democratic primary for a state Senate seat in 2002. He lost in the general election. Tracy was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2021/2/6/22270388/former-gaming-board-chair-picked-to-lead-illinois-gop" target="_blank" >narrowly elected state GOP chair</a> over pushback from hardline conservative leaders from rural areas downstate, where Trump remains immensely popular.</p><p>Tracy says he wants stricter border enforcement, upholding federal immigration laws and stronger support for law enforcement. He's also supportive of Trump's plan for a voter ID. </p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-6c0000" name="module-6c0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>What to Know - Races We’re Watching</h3><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9992ee02-bd07-11f1-93ab-21195d7ab2fe"><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-us-senate-race-juliana-stratton-don-tracy-dick-durbin" ><b>U.S. Senate</b></a>: Juliana Stratton, Don Tracy</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-4th-congressional-district-patty-garcia-chris-getty-lupe-castillo-ed-hershey-us-rep-jesus-chuy-garcia" ><b>U.S. Congress (4th District)</b></a>: Lupe Castillo, Patty García, Chris Getty, Ed Hershey</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-llinois-governor-race-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett" ><b>Governor</b></a>: Darren Bailey, Collin Corbett, JB Pritzker</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-candidates-race-illinois-attorney-general-kwame-raoul-bob-fioretti" ><b>Illinois Attorney General</b></a>: Robert Fioretti, Kwame Raoul</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-comptroller-race-bryan-drew-state-rep-margaret-croke" ><b>Illinois Comptroller</b></a>: Margaret Croke, Bryan Drew </li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-secretary-of-state-race-alexi-giannoulias-diane-harris" ><b>Illinois Secretary of State</b></a>: Alexi Giannoulias, Diane M. Harris</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-illinois-97th-house-district-race-jessica-dixon-heitman-gabby-shanahan" ><b>Illinois House (District 97)</b></a>: Jessica Dixon Heitman, Gabby Shanahan</li><li><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/illinois-statehouse-elections-november-3-senate-house-general-assembly-what-to-know" ><b>More Illinois House Races</b></a></li></ul></div> </div><p></p>
